10950.context: Sociologically, time use surveys show that societies allowing individuals to self-direct their schedules report markedly higher life satisfaction and productivity. Clear evidence that owning your priorities matters. Psychologically, Locke and Latham's goal setting theory reveals that when you clearly define and own your priorities, you amplify focus, motivation, and well-being, turning fuzzy wishes into actionable plans.

7419.context: I don't believe in your God. I used to believe in God, but I no longer do. And quite often people will ask me why I don't believe in God. And I don't always give the same answers because there isn't just one answer. I could say that I don't see the Bible lining up with reality, or that Christians are supposed to have the evidence of the fruit of the spirit, but I rarely saw that evidence. I could say that I've had way too many unanswered prayers. I could talk about how the problem of evil makes a good God who is also all powerful impossible in this world we currently live in.

claims.text: The term 'evidence' is used to establish a standard of proof against which religious claims, such as those concerning Jesus' existence and supernatural attributes, are measured (L2, L3).

The speaker uses 'evidence' repeatedly to contrast objective reality with subjective emotional states or tradition (L5, L16). It is employed rhetorically to define a standard of belief that must supersede emotion and convenience (L5, L16).
The term 'evidence' functions as a necessary standard for evaluating supernatural or religious claims, requiring verifiable proof.

The term 'evidence' is used as a standard against which beliefs and worldviews are measured for intellectual integrity (L13). It also functions as a necessary component for critical thinking, allowing individuals to revise their understanding when new information becomes available (L2, L8).

The speaker uses 'evidence' rhetorically to distinguish between genuine knowledge and unverified claims (L9, L16). It is also employed to define a healthy approach to belief, emphasizing that it must guide action rather than being ignored in favor of emotion or tradition (L5, L6).
